summary: Batch job pause/resume caused partial-hour prorate applied to reserved rate on invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed an unexpected partial-hour prorate on their monthly invoice after pausing a long-running batch embeddings job for ~18 minutes and then resuming it. Impact: invoice shows a blended reserved/hourly charge that is higher than expected for the dedicated commit they purchased. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-ukr-3) attached to MatterWave account in us-east-1, batch job submitted via /v1/batch-embed endpoint using API key scoped to dedicated pool.

Customer expectation: When a job runs under a reserved capacity commit, it should consume reserved capacity hours for the minute-level duration the job actually used; brief pauses that don't change queue assignment should not trigger an hourly repricing or partial-hour prorate that results in higher cost.

Observed behavior: Job was running from 2026-03-02 14:12:00 to 2026-03-02 16:45:00 with an 18-minute pause 15:23:40 to 15:41:40. Invoice shows two line items: 14:00-15:00 reserved-rate, then 15:00-16:00 a blended 'reserved+on-demand' prorated line where the pause period appears to have caused the billing engine to apply an on-demand rate for a slice of the hour, leading to an unexpected $420 delta.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running batch embed job routed to a dedicated pool under an active reserved commit
2) Pause the job for ~15-20 minutes via the batch control API (customer used a client-side pause that pauses enqueuing of microbatches)
3) Resume the job and allow it to complete within the same hourly window,
4) Run invoice preview for that billing window and compare line item assignment for reserved vs on-demand pricing
logs: Batch worker logs (excerpt): 2026-03-02T15:23:40Z - client paused enqueue; 2026-03-02T15:41:40Z - client resumed enqueue
Billing engine trace: billing-event: 2026-03-02T15:00:01Z - allocation reassessed for dedicated-ukr-3; flagged 00:41:40-01:00:00 as partial non-reserved slice (trace id be-5512)
Metering postback: POST /billing/postback returned 200 for microbatch windows 15:00-15:10/15:10-15:20/... last slice 15:40-15:50 with sequence gaps at 15:24 and 15:41
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: queue rebalancer considers 'paused' tasks as inactive and triggers a temporary release of reserved slots causing short on-demand allocation; the billing aggregation then treated resumed slices as separate allocation windows.

Checked scheduler logs: at 15:23:41 scheduler marked job_8891 as 'paused-client', and at 15:41:40 state transitioned to 'active' with new allocation id alloc_22b. Allocation change coincided with billing re-eval window for 15:00-16:00.

Reviewed billing aggregation job: hourly window aggregator merges allocation tags per-minute; a gap in postbacks (client-side pause) produced an allocation boundary which our merge logic currently treats as 'unallocated' => falls back to on-demand.
Reproduction in staging: recreated pause/resume scenario with synthetic microbatches routed to a reserved pool; staging invoice preview shows same blended line item behavior.

Related-priority: links to SUP-30192 (overnight credits double-counted during batch run) due to both involving batch postback ordering; billing PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/771 touches hourly aggregation logic.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 - Customer (Ana @ MatterWave): 'We paused a large batch for 18 minutes to address a downstream DB hiccup. We expected reserved pricing for the full run because our dedicated pool was active the whole time. The invoice shows a $420 unexpected charge. Please advise.'
2026-03-10 - Support (Maya): 'Thanks Ana — we're looking into allocation boundaries and billing windows. We'll validate with engineering and update within 24 hours.'

2026-03-11 - Eng (Liam): 'Found aggregation gap; reproducer validated in staging. Next step: patch merge to treat short client-side pauses as continuous allocation if same allocation id persists or paused duration < 30 minutes. Draft PR created.'

2026-03-12 - Support (Maya): 'We plan to issue a provisional credit while engineering prepares the fix and a retrospective invoice adjustment if confirmed. Will share once fix is merged and replayed.'
workaround: Advise customer to use server-side pause (batch control API 'hold' which retains allocation) instead of client-side enqueue pause where possible
If pause unavoidable, aim to resume within 5 minutes to avoid allocation rebalancer boundary in current system
Support can provisionally credit affected invoice line on a case-by-case basis pending engineering fix
resolution: Temporary resolution: provisional credit of $420 issued to MatterWave account on 2026-03-12 (credit memo CM-20260312-8891).
Permanent fix: engineering to merge patch to billing aggregator to treat allocation id continuity as primary signal and ignore sub-hour gaps under 30 minutes when allocation id unchanged (PR #771).

Follow-up actions: run a backfill/aggregation replay job for March 2 billing window to correct any other affected accounts; update Confluence runbook 'Batch Billing Prorate Rules' to document pause semantics.
Postmortem planned: if backfill triggers >$5k adjustments, escalate to finance and send notice to customers affected.
comments: Liam (Engineering) 2026-03-11: 'Patch branch ready: billing/agg: treat contiguous allocation id as continuous even if postback gap <= 30m unless explicit deallocation event present. Need QA run in staging then one-week canary.'
Maya (Support) 2026-03-12: 'Credit applied and customer confirmed receipt. Leaving ticket open until backfill completes and PR lands.'
Ana (Customer) 2026-03-12: 'Thanks — credit received and billing note is helpful. We'll switch to server-side hold for critical runs in the meantime.'
